The aim of this opportunity is to collect and create a waste tire treatment facility for the entire Al Jouf cluster.

Nearly one billion ELTs are generated worldwide annually, 
constituting more than 2% of the total amount of solid waste, 
and this waste flow is growing dynamically

The operation would require a stable input of end-of-life tires 
from producers for processing the waste

The rise in personal wealth and transforming 
consumer behavior in the Kingdom (increasing 
digitization, increasing personal consumption etc.) 
are increasing tire consumption requiring uplift in 
waste treatment solutions 

Waste management sector transformation driven 
by the Vision 2030 and initiatives to increase 
private sector participation require innovative, and 
sustainable solutions in KSA

The high level of economic and population growth in the KSA 
is expected to generate significant increase in consumption 
over the coming years, thus creating an opportunity for an 
end-of-life tire treatment facility operator to enter an attractive 
market

The Kingdom is placing a significant focus on the waste 
management sector as part of the Vision 2030 and the project 
can expect high level of engagement from the relevant 
authorities 
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 2M USD*

Plant capacity: 3,600 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 8.17 years




raw.title: AL BAHA CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment and final disposal operator, offering services in Al Baha

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Al Baha's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 1.97M USD*

Plant capacity: 150,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6.93 years

GDP Impact: 32M USD

Location (Region): Al Baha

full_description.raw:
The project is aiming to establish construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment and final disposal operator, offering services in Jazan

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Jazan's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.57M USD*

Plant capacity: 150,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6.88 years

GDP Impact: 37M USD

Location (Region): Jazan

raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Northern Borders.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Northern Borders 's population growth and 
expansion are the main drivers of construction and 
demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions

M USD

Expected Investment size: 2.1M USD*

Plant capacity: 346,994 tons

Expected IRR: 10.3%






full_description.raw:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Northern Borders.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Northern Borders 's population growth and 
expansion are the main drivers of construction and 
demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 2.1M USD*

Plant capacity: 346,994 tons

Expected IRR: 10.3%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 34M USD

Location (Region): Northern Borders

raw.title: NORTHEN BORDERS CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 2
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Northern Borders
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Northern Borders's population growth and 
expansion are the main drivers of construction 
and demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and 
government incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the 
development of the infrastructure sector, which 
is expected to lead to an increase in waste 
generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD

Location (Region): Northern Borders

full_description.raw:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Northern Borders

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Northern Borders's population growth and 
expansion are the main drivers of construction and 
demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD

Location (Region): Northern Borders

raw.title: YANBU INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Yanbu.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Yanbu's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions

M USD 

Expected Investment size: 1.7M USD*

Plant capacity: 295,291 tons

Expected IRR: 10.3%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 29M USD

Location (Region): Yanbu

raw.title: YANBU CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 2
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Yanbu
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Yanbu's population growth and expansion are 
the main drivers of construction and 
demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and 
government incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the 
development of the infrastructure sector, 
which is expected to lead to an increase in 
waste generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD


full_description.raw:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Yanbu
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Yanbu's population growth and expansion are 
the main drivers of construction and 
demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and 
government incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the 
development of the infrastructure sector, 
which is expected to lead to an increase in 
waste generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD

Location (Region): Yanbu

raw.title: HAFAR ALBATIN INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Hafar Al Batin.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Hafar Al Batin’s population growth and expansion 
are the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 1.7M USD*

Plant capacity: 282,585 tons

Expected IRR: 10.3%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 28M USD

Location (Region): Hafar Al Batin

full_description.raw:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Hafar Al Batin.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Hafar Al Batin’s population growth and expansion 
are the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 1.7M USD*

Plant capacity: 282,585 tons

Expected IRR: 10.3%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 28M USD

Location (Region): Hafar Al Batin

raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Hafar Al Batin
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Hafar Al Batin’s population growth and 
expansion are the main drivers of construction 
and demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and 
government incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the 
development of the infrastructure sector, which 
is expected to lead to an increase in waste 
generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years




full_description.raw:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Al Qunfudhah
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Al Qunfudhah's population growth and expansion 
are the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD

Location (Region): Al Qunfundah

raw.title: AL KHARJ INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Al Kharj.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Al Kharj's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 2.2M USD*

Plant capacity: 366,419 tons

Expected IRR: 10.33%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 36M USD


full_description.raw:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Al Kharj.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Al Kharj's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 2.2M USD*

Plant capacity: 366,419 tons

Expected IRR: 10.33%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 36M USD

Location (Region): Al Kharj

raw.title: AL KHARJ CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 2
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Al Kharj
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Al Kharj's population growth and expansion 
are the main drivers of construction and 
demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and 
government incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the 
development of the infrastructure sector, 
which is expected to lead to an increase in 
waste generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD


raw.title: TABUK CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 2
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Tabuk
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Tabuk's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD

Location (Region): Tabuk


The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected

total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Al Qassim's population growth and expansion are 
the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions

raw.title: AL QASSIM CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 2
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Al Qassim
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Al Qassim's population growth and expansion 
are the main drivers of construction and 
demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and 
government incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the 
development of the infrastructure sector, which 
is expected to lead to an increase in waste 
generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD

Location (Region): Al Qassim

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected


Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Dawadmi's population growth and expansion are 
the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

necessitating further waste management solutions

raw.title: DAWADMI CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 2
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Dawadmi
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Dawadmi's population growth and expansion are 
the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 5.33M USD*

Plant capacity: 600,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 162M USD

Location (Region): Dawadmi

raw.title: AL AHSA INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Al Ahsa.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Al Ahsa's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions

M USD 

Expected Investment size: 5.1M USD*

Plant capacity: 865,840 tons

Expected IRR: 10.3%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 85M USD


raw.title: AL AHSA CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 3
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Al Ahsa

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Al Ahsa's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Project is expected to have a stable supply of input material 
and a strong investment returns relative to peers in other 
geographies due to high number of construction projects 
expected in the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 5.33M USD*

Plant capacity: 600,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 162M USD


The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020.

of the total waste produced worldwide and is

demolition coming from private CDW collectors


main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation


incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD

expected in the Kingdom

raw.title: TAIF INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Taif.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Taif's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and 
government incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the 
development of the infrastructure sector, which 
is expected to lead to an increase in waste 
generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 3.2M USD*

Plant capacity: 538,157 tons

Expected IRR: 10.3%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 53M USD

Location (Region): Taif

raw.title: TAIF CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 2
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Taif
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Taif's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 5.33M USD*

Plant capacity: 600,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 162M USD

Location (Region): Taif

raw.title: MEDINAH INERT LANFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Medina.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Medina's population growth and expansion are 
the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and 
government incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the 
development of the infrastructure sector, which 
is expected to lead to an increase in waste 
generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 6.5M USD*

Plant capacity: 1,091,927 tons

Expected IRR: 10.3%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 108M USD

Location (Region): Medina

raw.title: MEDINAH CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 4
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Medina
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Medina's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Project is expected to have a stable supply of input material 
and a strong investment returns relative to peers in other 
geographies due to high number of construction projects 
expected in the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 5.33M USD*

Plant capacity: 600,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 162M USD

Location (Region): Medina

raw.title: MEDINAH CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 3
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Medina

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Medina's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Project is expected to have a stable supply of input material 
and a strong investment returns relative to peers in other 
geographies due to high number of construction projects 
expected in the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 5.33M USD*

Plant capacity: 600,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 162M USD

Location (Region): Medina


The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Makkah's population growth and expansion are the main 
drivers of construction and demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development of the 
infrastructure sector, which is expected to lead to an 
increase in waste generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the project is 
looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector with limited existing 
competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has significant 
support within the Kingdom

Project is expected to have a stable supply of input material and a strong 
investment returns relative to peers in other geographies due to high 
number of construction projects expected in the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 5.33M USD*

Plant capacity: 600,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 


raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Makkah
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Makkah's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Project is expected to have a stable supply of input material 
and a strong investment returns relative to peers in other 
geographies due to high number of construction projects 
expected in the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 5.33M USD*

Plant capacity: 600,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 162M USD


necessitating further waste management solutions

raw.title: JEDDAH CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 11
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Jeddah
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 5.33M USD*

Plant capacity: 600,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 162M USD

Location (Region): Jeddah

GCC water quality monitors (excl. KSA)
KSA water quality monitors
•
MEWA mandates wastewater, industrial, and 
desalination plants to monitor and report discharged 
water quality
•
Water production, storage, and transmission projects in 
pipeline are valued at SAR ~2203 Mn according to MEED 
•
NCEC’s push for 100% registration of entities with 
environmental impact is driving increased demand
•
Global market is growing at a CAGR of ~5%, driven by stricter 
regulatory compliance, increasing industrial demand, and growing 
environmental awareness
•
IoT-enabled sensors provide real-time data on key parameters such as 
pH, turbidity, and contaminants
•
Automated systems and robotics, including remote sampling, improve 
data accuracy and reduce costs by efficiently collecting samples from 
challenging locations
•
Nanotechnology has been instrumental in enhancing the sensitivity and 
selectivity of water quality sensors, allowing for the detection of 
emerging contaminants
Raw materials required for the manufacturing of water quality 
monitoring equipment include, but are not limited to: 
•
Platinum
•
Copper
•
Glass 
•
Plastics / polymers 
•
Silicon 
•
Gold / Silver
Components of water quality monitors that will be assembled at 
proposed facility include, but are not limited to:
•
Electrodes
•
Temperature probes
•
Displays
•
Flow cells
•
Signal processors 
•
Calibration controls

raw.title: Manufacturing of air quality monitoring equipment
raw.description:
The investment entails establishing a facility for the assembly of air quality monitoring equipment
•
Demand in KSA is estimated at SAR ~240 Mn, accounting for ~40% GCC 
demand and expected to grow 3x by 2030
•
Supply is ~ 100% imports dependent, with only two assemblers having 
limited utilization in KSA market 
•
In addition to the industrial market, presence of over 240 air 
monitoring stations drives demand through upgrades
•
Facility set up is supported by industrial zones providing access to 
facilities and utilities
•
Global air quality monitoring equipment market is growing at a CAGR 
of ~ 7%, driven by public and private sector initiatives to reduce air 
pollution 
•
Market is characterized by a mix of established multinational 
companies and specialized regional firms
•
Demand is rising for portable air quality monitors and comprehensive 
solutions that measure multiple pollutants simultaneously
•
Increasing integration of IoT sensors (e.g., CEMS) and ambient air 
quality systems into smart city infrastructure

•
Environmental compliance auditing market is estimated at SAR ~ 400 
Million and is expected to grow ~ 9x by 2030
•
Limited local coverage across emerging sectors such as hydrogen, 
renewable energy, mining, and advanced manufacturing
•
Expected Investment size of SAR ~ 10 Million
•
Expected IRR: ~ 26% for the 10-year IRR
•
Payback period: 4.7 years
•
Location: Central region, Western region, and Eastern region
•
NCEC is targeting 100% registration of entities with 
environmental impact, driving demand for 
environmental compliance audits
•
Upcoming spend of SAR ~3,4602 Bn and SAR ~5502 Bn in 
construction and manufacturing projects respectively, 
will drive demand for environmental assessments
•
NCEC has published clear standards and requirements 
for submitting audit reports, mandating entities to 
provide an audit report as a pre-requisite for the renewal 
of the environmental permit to operate
•
The market is at an evolving stage, with demand expected to grow 
rapidly (37% YoY) in coming years, presenting an attractive opportunity 
for new entrants
•
Currently, there are over 80 service providers in the market; however, 
their capacity remains insufficient to meet the rapidly growing demand
•
Global environmental compliance auditing market is growing at a CAGR 
of ~ 7%, primarily driven by stricter regulatory compliance, and growing 
reporting on sustainability by leading public companies
•
Inclusion of ESG metric disclosures as part of the assessment framework
•
Integration of advanced digital technologies, such as AI and machine 
learning, in assessment processes
•
Incorporation of social dimensions by engaging indigenous and local 
communities in assessments

Environmental laboratory testing market in KSA is estimated at SAR ~

•
KSA is a global leader in desalinated water production, with SWA 
operating 30 desalination plants, contributing to increased demand for 
laboratory testing for water quality
•
National efforts to boost environmental remediation market will also 
drive growth in laboratory testing services

There is a significant gap in specialized environmental testing in KSA, as 
no local laboratory currently offers radioactivity and Persistent Organic 
Pollutants (POP) testing
•
Expected Investment size of SAR ~ 40 Million
•
Expected IRR: ~ 16% for the 10-year IRR
•
Payback period: 6.0 years
•
Location: Central region, Western region, and Eastern region
•
Desalination and water treatment projects are driving 
demand for lab testing with an investment pipeline of 
SAR ~ 2202 Bn in water projects 
•
Investment pipeline in O&G and mining (SAR 7502 Bn) 
and manufacturing (SAR 5532 Bn) is expected to drive 
demand for soil testing
•
Soil testing market is nascent, with growth expected as 
NCEC standards introduced in 2021 become increasingly 
enforced
•
Market is at evolving stage, with demand expected to grow rapidly 
(19% YoY) in coming years, presenting an attractive opportunity for 
new entrants
•
Only ~30 service providers are licensed for environmental laboratory 
testing with over 80% being local entities
•
Absence of local laboratories that currently offer specialized 
environmental testing
•
Global market is growing at a CAGR of ~ 7%, driven by stringent 
government, rapid industrialization, and the development of advanced 
testing procedures
•
Market is characterized by a mix of multinational companies and 
specialized regional firms
•
Demand for mobile and on-site testing solutions is growing
•
Expanded testing scope is driven by emerging regulations and 
increased awareness of contaminants, such as PFAS and microplastics

raw.title: MURABBA MAKKAH – KAKIYYAH DISTRICT, MAKKAH
raw.description: Murabba Makkah is aimed to be a mixed-use development with 5-star hotel and a commercial mall components.The land is located in Kakiyyah District, along Ibrahim Al-Khalil Road that directly connects with Haram at 5.5km at 15mins drive, 9km from Mina-Arafat, 3km from Thaur Cave and approx. 10km from Jeddah-Makkah Expressway.The site lies in the residential district of Kakiyyah and has access to all infrastructure utilities including Electricity, Sewerage, Road and Telecommunication network.The location is well connected with all major historical sites, major commercial malls and has abundance of public transport that makes commutation easy.

raw.title: Manufacturing Of Mechanical Seals For Industrial Equipment
raw.description: This opportunity entails developing the value chain for the production of mechanical seals for industrial equipment to serve KSA and the broader GCC region.Overall demand for mechanical seals in Saudi Arabia has been growing, estimated to be 19,000 units in 2017. Driven by upcoming energy projects by Saudi Aramco, SEC and SWCC, demand is forecasted to increase at an annual growth rate of 6.1% to reach 30,300 units by 2025. Currently, KSA demand for mechanical seals for industrial equipment is addressed mainly domestically; however, the remaining 30% is addressed through imports, presenting a great opportunity for investors to localize production.Beyond the KSA market, investors in Saudi have the opportunity to tap into the larger regional market in the GCC. With a growing demand in the region for high-quality mechanical seals used in oil and gas, water and wastewater, and power projects, the demand in the rest of the GCC is expected to increase from 29,000 units in 2017 to 45,000 units by 2025.In addition to an increasing market demand, Saudi Arabia has competitive costs for materials, labor and logistics and offers funding and incentives to investors.The main focus of this opportunity is to establish a manufacturing facility for mechanical seals for industrial equipment.Manufacturing: establish mechanical seals manufacturing facility to fabricate seals components, the facility to include turning, boring, grooving, milling, drilling and tapping capabilitiesFinishing operations: establish workshops to deliver hard facing, grinding, lapping, polishing and welding capabilities in addition to advanced surface treatment proceduresHowever, additional opportunities for localization exist across the value chain of mechanical seals production. These opportunities include:Design: establish a design and engineering capabilitiesInput materials: establish local foundriesInstallation and maintenance: offer support services, including quality control, assembly, and installation servicesInstallation and maintenance: offer maintenance services and repair services for mechanical seals and installed base

raw.title: Manufacturing Of Circuit Breakers
raw.description: This opportunity entails developing the value chain for the production of circuit breakers to serve KSA and the broader GCC region.The overall demand for circuit breakers in Saudi Arabia has been growing, estimated at USD 370 million in 2018. Driven by utilities, oil and gas and other manufacturing industries, KSA demand is forecasted to increase at an annual growth rate of 4% to reach USD 439 million by 2022. In 2018, demand for circuit breakers is 60% for high voltage and 30% for low voltage and ~10% for medium voltage. The split is expected to remain relatively the same till 2022.Beyond the KSA market, investors in Saudi have the opportunity to tap into the large regional market in the GCC with expected increase in demand from USD 308 million in 2018 to USD 370 million by 2022.The focus of this opportunity is on final manufacturing and components manufacturing of circuit breakers. These opportunities entail:Components manufacturing: establish manufacturing facilities conductors, contacts, operating mechanism and enclosuresFinal manufacturing and testing: establish facilities for final manufacturing of low circuit breakersFinal manufacturing and testing: establish facilities for final manufacturing of medium voltage circuit breakersFinal manufacturing and testing: establish world scale testing facilities for (e.g., vacuum interrupter predictive testing)However, there are additional opportunities across the circuit breakers manufacturing value chain. Opportunities include:Design: custom design and engineer circuit breakers for low and medium voltage applications for Saudi customersInput materials: manufacture copper alloys to meet KSA's specifications

raw.title: Manufacturing Of Industrial Gears
raw.description: This opportunity entails developing the value chain for the production of gears for industrial machinery to serve KSA and the broader GCC region.The overall demand for industrial gears in Saudi Arabia has been growing, estimated at USD 97 million in 2017. Driven by the presence of several oil and gas manufacturing companies in the Kingdom, market size is forecasted to increase at an annual growth rate of 3% to reach USD 121 million by 2025. The global gears market is dominated by spur gears and bevel gears, having 50-80% market share.Beyond the KSA market, investors in Saudi have the opportunity to tap into the wider regional market of the GCC. With many companies in the GCC establishing extraction and production plants, demand for gears in the region has been increasing and is expected to continue to increase from USD 106 million in 2017 to USD 151 million by 2025.The main focus of this opportunity is to establish a manufacturing facility for industrial gears.Manufacturing: establish outsourced services offering heat treatment, machining…Manufacturing: establish facilities to produce locally and supply manufacturing facilitiesHowever, additional opportunities for localization exist across the value chain of industrial gears production. These opportunities include:Design: potential to be part of a larger design center setup by the EPC or the OEMRaw materials: localize production of key materials such as PEEK, Delrin, brass, etc.Operations and maintenance: offer support services, including maintenance, installation and operation services

raw.title: Up-Scale Hotel Towers and Premium Commercial (Office) Towers – Dar Al Hijrah

details.description:
Description of Investment Opportunity
Rua Al Madinah Holding, a PIF company, is a key driver in developing infrastructure and assets that enhance Madinah’s position as a premier destination with a contemporary architectural landscape.

As part of this mandate, Rua Al Madinah Holding is offering investment opportunities in three upscale hotel towers and four upscale commercial towers, located within the Dar Al Hijrah project, a landmark mixed-use urban development in the holy city of Madinah, Saudi Arabia.

 

Deal Structure

Flexible deal structures are available, with multiple partnership models such as joint ventures, real estate funds, investment consortia and land or building leases

Assets Under Consideration

Hotel Towers (Shell & Core)

Opportunity 1: ~380 keys, BUA +40,300 sqm, 3 basements + ground floor + 19 floors
Opportunity 2: ~380 keys, BUA +40,300 sqm, 3 basements + ground floor + 19 floors
Opportunity 3: ~614 keys, BUA ≈70,000 sqm, 2 basements + ground floor + 19 floors
Commercial (Office) Towers (Shell & Core)

Opportunity 4: BUA +72,250 sqm, land +10,650 sqm, 3 basements + ground floor + 11 floors
Opportunity 5: BUA +72,250 sqm, land +9,500 sqm, 3 basements + ground floor + 11 floors
Opportunity 6: BUA +72,250 sqm, land +13,380 sqm, 3 basements + ground floor + 11 floors
Opportunity 7: BUA +56,300 sqm, land +8,850 sqm, 3 basements + ground floor + 16 floors
Investor Participation

Investors may participate in one or more of these opportunities

raw.title: Local Manufacturing of Biologics

details.description: This opportunity involves setting up manufacturing facilities for biologic drugs in Saudi Arabia. Biologics are advanced therapies derived from living organisms, used to treat complex diseases such as cancer, autoimmune conditions, and rare disorders. Localizing production enhances healthcare innovation, quality of care, and biopharma sector competitiveness.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Accelerate the development of high-value biopharmaceutical manufacturing.
• Support healthcare innovation and access to advanced therapies.
• Reduce dependence on costly biologic imports.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: • Rising demand for biologics in oncology and autoimmune disease management. • Global shift toward precision medicine and advanced therapies. • Government support for high-tech pharma investment. • Strategic potential for regional leadership in biologics manufacturing.

raw.title: Production of Pharmaceutical Key Starting Materials (KSMs)

details.description: This opportunity seeks to localize the production of Key Starting Materials (KSMs), which are the essential building blocks in the production of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). It is a foundational investment that strengthens the upstream pharmaceutical supply chain, reduces dependency on imports, and contributes to long-term national health security.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Strengthen the upstream pharmaceutical manufacturing value chain.
• Reduce reliance on global suppliers for critical raw materials.
• Promote local R&D and industrial innovation.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: • Growing demand for localized pharmaceutical input production. • Support from the government for industrial diversification and healthcare security. • Potential for vertical integration with API and drug product manufacturers. • Opportunity to attract global partnerships and advanced manufacturing technologies.

raw.title: Local Manufacturing of Ophthalmology & ENT Diagnostic Devices

details.description: Establish local manufacturing of ophthalmoscopes and related ophthalmology and ENT diagnostic devices used for retinal, optic nerve, and ENT examinations. Targeted products include ophthalmoscopes, tonometers, ENT units, keratometers, otoscopes, tympanometry equipment, and more.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Healthcare Self-Sufficiency: Reducing reliance on imported medical equipment strengthens domestic supply chains and emergency preparedness.
• Growth Potential: Positions Saudi Arabia for strategic OEM partnerships in optical devices and enables expansion of local manufacturing capabilities.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: • Rising cases of vision complications (e.g., glaucoma, cataracts, diabetic retinopathy) increasing demand for advanced eye diagnostic solutions. • Growing access to vision care services and awareness boosting demand for portable and reliable diagnostic tools.

raw.title: Local Manufacturing of Intraocular Lenses (IOLs)

• Lay the foundation for innovation in advanced optics, including premium IOLs, presbyopia correction, and personalized lens designs.

raw.title: Local Manufacturing of Renal Care Devices

details.description: Establish local manufacturing of hemodialysis machines and dialyzers—critical components for renal care systems supporting patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Targeted products include artificial kidney (dialysis) apparatus, dialyzers, peritoneal dialysis units, and CRRT systems.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Enhance availability of critical products and reduce long-term procurement costs.
• Strengthen national healthcare preparedness through local supply.
• Advance MedTech sector by positioning Saudi Arabia in precision mechatronics and patient monitoring technology.

keyGrowthDrivers.description: • High and growing prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) across the population. • Increased hospital and clinic capacity driving demand for renal care devices. • Rising burden of non-communicable diseases requiring long-term dialysis treatments.

raw.title: Orthopedic Products Manufacturing

details.description: Establish local manufacturing of orthopedic products to support both surgical and non-surgical treatments of musculoskeletal conditions. Targeted products include head and spine orthopedic appliances, artificial joints, prosthetics, bionics, and orthotics.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Localize high-cost, high-precision devices to enhance accessibility and cost efficiency.
• Reduce dependency on imported orthopedic devices by manufacturing domestically.
• Position Saudi Arabia as a MedTech hub for sophisticated orthopedic solutions with regional export potential.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: • Rising musculoskeletal conditions driving demand for artificial joints and trauma implants. • Vision 2030 initiatives pushing to increase local content across healthcare and MedTech sectors. • Growth in surgical infrastructure and rehabilitation services.

raw.title: Local Manufacturing of Respiratory and Oxygen Therapy Devices

details.description: Establish local manufacturing of respiratory and oxygen therapy devices to support critical care and chronic disease management. This includes ventilators, CPAP, BiBAP, NO delivery systems, and devices for oxygen, ozone, and aerosol therapy. The opportunity targets hospitals, ICUs, emergency services, and home care environments.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Reduce reliance on imported medical equipment and build local manufacturing capacity.
• Strengthen national healthcare resilience, particularly for emergency and ICU settings.
• Support chronic respiratory disease management including asthma, COPD, and sleep apnea.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: • High prevalence of respiratory conditions in the population. • Demand for modular and multi-purpose devices across different care settings. • Expansion of hospital infrastructure and critical care investments. • Potential for exports through regional medtech manufacturing leadership.

raw.title: Local Manufacturing of Minimally Invasive Devices & Tools

details.description: Establish local manufacturing for minimally invasive medical tools and devices such as disposable endoscopes, laparoscopic instruments, energy platforms, and associated consumables. The opportunity targets supplying healthcare providers with advanced surgical solutions that enhance precision, reduce recovery time, and improve patient outcomes.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Strengthen domestic healthcare self-sufficiency by reducing reliance on imported medical equipment.
• Enhance national emergency preparedness and supply chain resilience.
• Position KSA as a MedTech manufacturing hub with regional export potential and partnerships with OEMs.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: • Rising demand from hospitals and surgical centers for minimally invasive procedures and tools. • National push to increase local content across strategic sectors, including MedTech. • Development of patient care devices as part of healthcare transformation goals.

raw.title: Assembly of Aviation Oil Lubricant Manufacturer

details.description:
Develop a Saudi-based aviation lubricant production facility to reduce reliance on imports.

 Partner with APSCO, ExxonMobil, and Aramco/Luberef to leverage global expertise and local manufacturing capabilities.

 Target a guaranteed domestic market (airlines, MROs, military aviation) and explore export opportunities in GCC & MENA.

 Enhance Saudi Arabia’s supply chain resilience by ensuring a stable, cost-effective lubricant supply.

Support Vision 2030 localization goals by reducing financial leakage and creating local jobs.

This Opportunity reduces financial leakage, enhances supply chain security, and creates a new industrial sector in Saudi Arabia. By localizing aviation lubricant production, this project can drive economic growth, reduce costs for airlines, and position Saudi Arabia as a regional hub for aviation lubricants.
Vision 2030 and the National Aviation Strategy set an ambitious target for the sector to grow from 100 Mn pax in 2019 to 330 Mn pax by 2030

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Currently there are no local assembly Aviation lubricant relying on international imports from one sources ( Exxon Mobile Texas plant)
• RTGs; potential to replace KSA imports

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: Cost Efficiency – Reduce import costs, shipping fees, and foreign currency risks. Operational Security – Ensure uninterrupted lubricant availability for commercial & military aviation. Economic Impact – Create local jobs, develop industrial expertise, and drive investment. Supply Chain Optimization – Eliminate logistics bottlenecks & price volatility. Sustainability & ESG Alignment – Support green aviation initiatives with localized, optimized production. KSA aviation sector to grow from 100Mn pax in 2019 to 330 Mn pax by 2030 KSA airlines’ fleet to grow from 250 aircrafts to 500 aircrafts Substantial regional demand from a strong aviation sector  Active players (non-exhaustive): International players: Exxon Mobile, Local Players: Apsco – Lubref/Aramco

raw.title: Adventure And Water Sport Activity Supplyer

details.description:
OPDC is seeking private sector investment and operational expertise to either JV or develop and manage a comprehensive range of water sports activities at THE RIG Project, a flagship tourism destination in Saudi Arabia. This opportunity allows private operators to provide services and equipment for various water sports while partnering with OPDC under a rent plus profit-sharing model. 

Products/services covered
- The opportunity targets a wide range of water sports and related services, including but not limited to:
- Adventure Water Sports: Kite surfing, surfing, jet skiing, e-foil rides, and motorized water sports.
- Recreational Water Sports: Diving, parasailing, snorkeling, and stand-up paddle boarding.
- Training Services: Professional lessons and certification for water sports enthusiasts.
- Rental Services: Equipment rentals for guests interested in independent water sport activities.
 
Focus of opportunity in the value chain

Upstream
- Investment in equipment and materials for water sports (e.g., jet skis, diving equipment, kite-boards).
- Recruitment and training of skilled personnel for operations and guest safety.
- Setting up operational hubs and storage facilities at “THE RIG”.

Midstream
- Service delivery, including providing water sports experiences, training, and rentals.
- Integration with “THE RIG’s” broader tourism offerings to enhance guest experiences.
- Adherence to OPDC’s standards for sustainability and safety.

Focus Area
- The opportunity is focused on offering a world-class, diverse water sports experience that complements the luxury tourism offerings at "THE RIG"

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• A unique opportunity to partner with a global tourism icon, a luxury, adventure-focused environment and become a vital part of the region's tourism evolution.
• OPDC is offering a lucrative rent plus profit-sharing model, enabling private sector players to generate consistent revenue without the need for significant upfront infrastructure investment.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - Saudi Arabia Adventure Tourism Market: Growing at 8-12% YoY. - GCC Water Sports Market: Growing at 6-8% YoY.  Mega Projects Boom – Government support tourism - High Demand for Experiences - Tourists are shifting towards unique, adrenaline-filled activities, creating demand for water sports such as kite surfing, e-foil, parasailing, and diving.

raw.title: Labor Accommodation - Rua Al Haram

details.description:
The Rua Al Haram development project presents a strategic investment opportunity for private investors to participate in the design, construction, and operation of logistics and labor accommodation facilities critical to the success of this large-scale, multi-phase development. These facilities will play a pivotal role in supporting the project's construction and operational activities, addressing workforce housing, material handling, and overall construction logistics.

Based on the current forecast (subject to change) of daily labor personnel numbers, the labor accommodation would have the following key characteristics:

- Land  – The land required is based upon 3-story residential buildings = 300m.sq x 600m.sq = 180,000 m.sq land area.
- Capacity required – The employee residential facilities would be required for ~ 5,000 employees consisting of:
      - 1 Bedroom (40 sq. m per room) – 8
      - 1 Bedroom (20m.sq per room) – 112
      - 2 Bed per room (20m.sq per room) – 280
      - 4 beds per room (24m.sq per room) – 1080

- Additional facilities include kitchens, dining, recreation, sport, laundry, admin, security, medical, retail, fire station, swimming pools, parking, and utilities. Additionally, other facilities, such as - compounds for contractors, consultants' offices, warehouses, off-site manufacturing, etc. (typically requiring ∼1,500 m.sq. for 200 people.

This opportunity targets essential infrastructure and operational services, including worker housing, transportation, material storage, batching plants, construction logistics, and security systems. These offerings are critical to supporting the smooth execution of the Rua Al Haram project and ensuring its timely delivery. They also create long-term value for investors through sustained demand and operational scalability.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• This opportunity offers strategic alignment with national priorities, financially lucrative revenue streams, and the chance to play a central role in one of the region's most significant urban development projects. By addressing critical project needs for logistics and labor accommodations, investors can secure a high-impact, low-risk position in a transformative initiative with long-term growth potential.
• The strategic benefits of this opportunity are rooted in the scale and complexity of the Rua Al Haram project, regional development priorities under Vision 2030, and technological and operational advancements that enhance efficiency and scalability. These benefits ensure sustained demand, long-term profitability, and expansion opportunities.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - Rua Al Haram represents the region's unparalleled urban development initiative, setting a new benchmark for scale and ambition. Its portfolio comprises of hotel guest rooms, residential units, commercial space, and prayer areas. - The project is expected to require a workforce of significant scale, reaching over 100,000 workers at peak construction.

raw.title: Residential and Retail Development Opportunities at Red Sea Project

details.description:
Deal Structure: Joint venture development partnership

Assets Under Consideration
- Luxury Residences: ~1,600 units.
- Luxury Retail and F&B Venues: 9,200 m².

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• The opportunity provides diverse retail and residential offerings which align with the spending habits of luxury travelers and residents. The opportunity targets the affluent consumer market for luxury residential and retail offerings in a prime tourist destination.
• The Red Sea Zone Authority is working to create Smart Destinations with state-of-the-art infrastructure, which enhance the attractiveness and accessibility for both residents and visitors.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - Increasing population and rising upper and middle-income segment point to a positive demand for luxury residential housing. - Surge in luxury tourism will drive further demand for residential, luxury retail and F&B experience, as visitors seek extended stays or consider secondary homes in the vicinity. - Strategic Location - the Red Sea is located north of Jeddah (~500 Km), and is within 8 hours flight time of 85% of the global population; further, newly created, dedicated airport will provide access and airlift to The Red Sea.

raw.title: KAFD Area 7

details.description:
KAFD has evolved to become a prime business and lifestyle destination capturing the core values of Vision 2030. KAFD empowers businesses through access to advanced office infrastructure and sustainable smart city solutions, while simultaneously offering unique lifestyle experiences with leading leisure and retail facilities. This opportunity focuses on residential assets for KAFD Area 7.

Deal Structure:
Joint venture future development  partnership

Assets Under Consideration:
Residential apartment products of a premium, luxury and branded nature. 
- Branded Residential Tower Parcels: 2 properties (354 units)
- Residential Tower Parcels: 4 properties (985 units)

strategicBenefitsPoints.point: • KAFD offers a world-class mixed use development and is the Financial and Business Center of Riyadh. This component will offer luxury and premium residential to the working population of KAFD’s offices as well as a spectrum of investors who wish to own property in the heart of the city.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - The opportunity targets the executive level employees of KAFD’s Grade A Office market and HNWI who wish to invest or keep residence adjacent to the Financial Center. - Strategic Location - Strategically located at the center of Riyadh and accessible via three main access points, including Northern Ring Road, King Fahd Road and Thumama Road. KAFD is also a strategic component of the Public Transport system with its Metro Station a central connection point for the three main lines of Riyadh City.

raw.title: TH Residential Community

details.description:
TH-3 is located in Murooj District, KAEC, Saudi Arabia (22.447770, 39.104484), next to Royal Greens Golf Course and AlMurooj Mall, and can be accessed via highway and Railway Network (public transportation).

Asset Type: Medium Density Residential - Villas and Townhouses.

Land Area: 179,220 sqm.

Gross Floor Area (GFA): 179,220 - 268,830 sqm.

Building Height: G+2 floors.

Site Access Date: Immediate.

Deal Structure: Land Sale in Cash or partnership.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Strategically located along the Red Sea, KAEC is poised to become one of the most important cities in the Middle East, serving global trade and international communities.
• Situated 90 km from the busiest airport in Saudi Arabia.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - KAEC’s strategic location maximizes its impact on the Red Sea, home to the second-largest port in the region. - Accessible to over 8.5 million people within a 78-minute train radius. - More than 30 million pilgrims are expected to visit KAEC by 2030.

raw.title: Northern Community 3 at Diriyah Gate II

details.description:
Northern Community 3 is a premium mixed-use district featuring high-end residential, Grade-A commercial offices, and vibrant retail offerings.

It aims to foster a vibrant urban community that targets affluent professionals, executives, and families seeking a connected, modern urban lifestyle.

Deal Structure 
- Land sale
 
Assets Under Consideration
- Residential apartments – 1,800 units with 80,000 sqm. land take and 180,000 sqm gross floor area (GFA)
- Commercial offices – Grade A offices with 20,000 sqm. land take and 50,000 sqm (GFA)
- Retail – 3,000 sqm. land take and 6,000 sqm (GFA)

strategicBenefitsPoints.point: • Diriyah – The City of Earth – has traditional Najdi architecture and offers a diverse hospitality offering across lifestyle, and luxury, branded residences to meet the needs of a broad spectrum of visitors. Its strategic location is accessible within minutes of key commercial districts of Riyadh and is a 25-minute-drive from King Khalid International Airport

raw.title: Urban Hotel Opportunity in a High-Growth Tourism Hub

details.description:
Hail is emerging as a key destination for cultural tourism and adventure seekers, offering experiences rooted in its rich history, vibrant community, and scenic landscapes.

Deal Structure: Joint Venture Development Partnership.

The investment opportunity includes:
- An Urban Hotel: 145-key hotel capturing the region’s heritage while providing world-class services.
- Authentic Souq: A traditional market showcasing local products and crafts.
- Family Entertainment: Indoor and outdoor attractions for all ages.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - Tourist Visit Growth: 54% CAGR in same-day trips (2015-2022), highlighting Hail’s rising popularity. - Increased Spending: 860% increase in tourist spending over the past five years. - Untapped Potential: Developing tourism infrastructure presents significant opportunities for early investors.  Investing in Hail offers high returns and aligns with Saudi Arabia’s growing tourism sector and Vision 2030.
